description:
FILED s415 while implementing Track A (#371).

TWO FINDINGS, one decision each.

(1) INDIRECT OBJECT was in Track A's refusal table (docs/option-b-phase2-plan.md
    Â§2, task #371) and was deliberately LEFT OUT after measuring where its drops
    are.  The whole census has exactly two:
      perl-tests/ref.t:334     $foo = doit $object "FOO";
      perl-tests/method.t:72   is((method $obj "a","b","c"), "method,a,b,c");
    (plus their t/op/ twins).  Those two files contribute 191 and 97 PASSING rows
    today, so refusing would cost ~288 perl-tests rows to convert 2 drops -- the
    opposite trade from the other five families, whose files are already
    unproductive.  And unlike given/when or smartmatch it is not a REMOVED
    feature: perl still parses it (only `no feature 'indirect'` is the 5.36
    default), so PCL could support it.
    DECISION NEEDED: implement the parse (an `is ref $u, ...`-shaped extent
    question, close to Track B), or refuse and pay the rows, or leave it
    dropping.  Nothing is urgent -- it is 2 drops.

(2) `class Foo;` (statement form, no block) is a SILENT WRONG today: it PARSES,
    as the indirect-object method call Foo->class, and emits
    (p-void-ctx (p-method-call (p-resolve-invocant "Foo") "class")).  It
    therefore never reaches the drop site, so #371's refusal cannot see it --
    the boundary that makes #371 safe (only already-lost statements) is exactly
    what lets this through.  The same is true of any 5.38 `class NAME;` file.
    Refusing it needs a rule OUTSIDE the drop site, which can break code: the
    shape is indistinguishable from the legitimate old indirect-object call, so
    the discriminator has to be `use feature 'class'` / `use v5.38+` in scope
    (Pl::Parser::_class_feature_in_scope already answers that question).
    That is a small, safe change -- but it is a new refusal on COMPILING code,
    so it needs the s372 gate-SET bar over both populations, which is why it is
    not in #371's commit.


=== HALF (b) DONE s417 â `class Foo;` no longer silently means Foo->class ===

RULED s416 (docs/fable-answers-s415.md Â§7.5) and shipped unchanged.  Half (a),
the indirect-object census drops in files with 288 passing rows, is UNTOUCHED
and this task stays open for it.

WHAT WAS MEASURED FIRST (all against perl 5.40.3):

  class Foo;                        perl DIES "Can't locate object method
                                    \"class\" via package \"Foo\"" -- so the
                                    indirect-object reading is RIGHT by default
                                    and PCL already matched it
  use feature 'class'; class Foo;   perl warns "class is experimental", RUNS
  use experimental 'class'; â¦       perl RUNS
  use v5.38; class Foo;             perl SYNTAX ERROR ("Bareword found where
                                    operator expected") -- so a version bundle
                                    can NEVER be evidence about code that
                                    compiles, exactly as the ruling said
  sub class {â¦} class Foo;          perl calls the user's sub

SHIPPED: `Pl::Parser::class_statement_refusal`, called at the top of
`Parser2::_lower_stmt`, dies perl-shaped when the file switched the feature on
EXPLICITLY (`use feature 'class'`, `use experimental 'class'`, or a
`class NAME { â¦ }` BLOCK elsewhere -- never the statement form itself, which
would be circular).  `_class_feature_in_scope` gained a `$strict` flag rather
than being copied, so the loose drop-site key (which DOES accept the bundle,
because there the statement is already lost) and the strict compiling-code key
cannot drift.

BAR MET (the s372 three legs, because a new refusal on compiling code):
  * corpus-diff: emission identical to HEAD across 111 files, drops 10 unchanged
  * gate-SET scan, BOTH populations, 638 files each: ZERO differences.  The two
    population files that use the statement form (t/class/class.t,
    t/class/field.t) already refused with the SAME message via their block
    form, which appears earlier in each file.
  * sweep: GATE clean, TOTAL 18369 (+0), drops 10 = census
  * five before/after probes against a worktree of the base commit: the two
    pragma spellings move from silent `Foo->class` to a refusal; `class Foo;`
    alone, `use v5.38; class Foo;` and the block form are UNCHANGED.
  * gate 153 files / 5590 rows (11 new), only the 13 pclxs xs rows.

GUARD: Pl/t/class-refusal-01.t (11 rows, 1.4 s -- transpile-only), including
every must-not-fire case the ruling named.


CLOSED s425 (Fable, 2026-08-22) â USER DECISION: MAYBE LATER.  Registered in docs/not-supported.md ("Indirect object syntax with a SCALAR invocant"), docs/STATUS.md row, README roadmap bullet.  Measured first: `new Foo`, `new Foo LIST`, `new Foo(LIST)`, `ref(new Foo)` already WORK (PExpr indirect-object pre-pass); corpus count of the constructor shape = cpan-tests 3 lines / perl t/ 3 / perl-tests 0 / lib 0, all working spellings.  The scalar-invocant spelling stays a loud drop (2 census rows); #381 stays open as the mis-compile.  Not refused (288 rows), not scheduled, cheapest after B3.  Finding (2) `class NAME ;` was done s417.
subject: Indirect object syntax: its two census drops sit in files with 288 passing rows -- decide, do not refuse blindly (Track A's excluded row); and a bare `class Foo;` is a SILENT WRONG (it parses as Foo->class)
